newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-MIM leaves j/v option open on Fisher.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-MIM leaves j/v option open on Fisher.

text.p: Base metals miner MIM Holdings Ltd said on Monday it was leaving its options open for managing its additional exposure to zinc if its George Fisher lead-zinc orebody near Mt Isa in north Queensland is developed.
"If George Fisher is developed, the company will be considering ways of managing its zinc exposure," MIM general manager, public affairs, Collin Myers told Reuters.
Myers declined to comment on media reports that MIM would consider introducing outside partners into the development of the A$250 million project, expected to begin next year.
MIM is currently considering a full feasability study on the 50 million-tonne orebody, formerly known as Hilton North.
MIM has allocated about A$23 million to a study of the Fisher project with a pre-feasability study already completed.
The deposit is being studied to see if it could be a successor to the group's Mt Isa lead-zinc mine which will be exhausted by the turn of the century.
George Fisher is considered to be a three to four million-tonne a year operation.
"Pasminco and Korea Zinc are two companies that could be interested in a joint venture at George Fisher," Wilson HTM Ltd research director, Phil Hutchings said.
Pasminco is a leading Australian producer while Korea Zinc is planning a major A$1 billion zinc refinery at Townsville by the year 2000.
